- Confirms the signing workflow (DocuSign attrs) for a post-signature exhibit — we want to avoid re-executing the entire DPA if possible.

B) an updated Exhibit B reissued as a cover amendment to the original DPA that your system recognizes as a re-execution?

If we can do (A) that would be simplest for our downstream compliance audit. If (B) is mandatory on your side, please outline the minimal fields we need to preserve to avoid a full re-execution (signers, envelope ids, effective date rules).

Would loop in your privacy counsel and ops to get this executed by next week.

Best,
María

High level: Redwood can accept a standalone supplemental exhibit signed by both parties (option A) in most cases, provided the exhibit references the original DPA by execution date and includes a clause that it is an amendment to Exhibit B. Thanks — quick technical note from legal:

1) Standalone supplemental (A) is acceptable. The exhibit must: reference the original DPA including signature date and original exhibit name/number; state that it amends Exhibit B; specify an effective date; and include an explicit signature block for each party.

2) DocuSign requirements to avoid re-execution hassles: preserve the original DPA's DocuSign envelope id in a cover page/field if there was one (helps our contract database map the amendment), and include the full signer names + job titles in the envelope. If your DocuSign system doesn't allow a single envelope, a separate envelope for the exhibit is fine but include a short cover note tying it to the original DPA (execution date + deal id).

3) For EU->US transfers we accept SCCs or a company-level transfer addendum. If InsightCloud relies on SCCs, please attach a copy and confirm whether InsightCloud will be data importer under the SCC template.

Laura — can you confirm if we need a separate privacy ops ticket for onboarding the subprocessor?

Karthik
Deputy Counsel, Redwood Inference
